summary: A checkpoint trim deletes the signature and verdict rows of the claims it drops, and sweeps the ones earlier trims left behind

replay.detail: No replay or projection rebuild. Verdicts of kept claims are unchanged; recheck_claim_verdicts reports no mismatch after a trim or the sweep.

schema.detail: No tables, columns, indexes, triggers or schema version change. The sweep records its progress in meta under checkpoint_trimmed_claim_rows_swept.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged; the same claims are dropped. The deleted rows are local caches outside the graph, authority and checkpoint digests, so trimmed, untrimmed and swept members still agree.

compatibility.detail: No client, wire or harness contract change. A new CheckpointAction variant, swept-trimmed-claim-rows, appears in the daemon log once per node when the sweep deletes rows.

downtime.detail: No restart requirement beyond the ordinary deploy. The one-time sweep runs in the background checkpoint pass in transactions that stop deleting after 20 ms. On a production copy it deleted 1,563,803 rows in 6,232 transactions over 392 s and freed 54,290 pages (222 MB of page bytes become free for reuse).

manual.detail: No manual step. The file does not shrink: SQLite reuses the freed pages.

recovery.detail: Binary rollback needs no store change; an older build simply leaves such rows behind again on later trims.
